chapters.title: 3 John
body: This letter is warm where 2 John was cautious — John writes with real delight about Gaius, specifically praised for faithfully welcoming traveling believers and strangers, people who'd "gone forth" for the gospel "taking nothing of the Gentiles." That concrete generosity, not abstract reputation, is what earns the commendation.

The contrast is just as specific: Diotrephes, who "loveth to have the preeminence," refuses to welcome the same travelers and even expels those who try — status-seeking actively working against the hospitality the gospel depended on. Demetrius gets a brief, simple good word in between. If hospitality toward people who cost you something has ever felt like a minor virtue, this short letter treats it as exactly the kind of faithfulness worth writing a whole letter to praise.
